campaignTrail_temp.election_json = [ { "model": "campaign_trail.election", "pk": 21, "fields": { "year": 2020, "summary": "

2016 seems like a lifetime ago. Since her win that year, President Clinton has had to govern over a series of divisive, and consequential, challenges including mass-shootings, racial tensions, corruption, corporate greed, and foreign disasters constantly restrained by a large Republican majority in the House.

Fresh into the new year, the 2020 election has been in the minds of establishment Republicans since November 9th, 2016. Trump, however, has brought up the ‘discrepancies’ of the 2016 election every chance he has gotten. And, following the GOP’s extensive victory in 2018, he was one of the first to announce his run for President. Trump was followed by over 2-dozen others in what is now seen as one of the largest, and somewhat divisive, Republican primaries for President ever, all unified behind one common goal– making Hillary Clinton a one-term President.

Clinton, still recovering from a smackdown in 2018, has had her legislative agenda held hostage by the Republican-controlled house since she was inaugurated. Still hoping to regain the country’s trust, she’ll have to give Congressional Republicans massive concessions if she wants to check off some of the things she promised before the election this fall.

As November nears, the President will have to weather serious attacks from those within her own party as well as the opposing party, a global pandemic, racial tensions, and a country not seen this divided for generations.

campaignTrail_temp.candidate_json = [ { "model": "campaign_trail.candidate", "pk": 41421, "fields": { "first_name": "Hillary", "last_name": "Clinton", "election": 21, "party": "Democrat", "state": "New York", "priority": 1, "description": "

Here we go. After just over three years of congressional gridlock stomping on some of the largest parts of your agenda, November will be the litmus test for how the country believes you have done as President. 2016 was closer than you expected, and now you must prove that you were not just a one-time thing. While you have secured some smaller bipartisan accomplishments in infrastructure, immigration, and trade, Congress has blocked nearly every major initiative you promised four years ago. Failed efforts on climate, taxes, and healthcare have left much of your agenda unfulfilled, while the compromises you have secured have alienated parts of your own party's progressive base. Once again, you will have to contend with the problem that has plagued your presidency from the beginning: partisanship. This will be the fight of your life, but given the last 30 years, you are prepared for what is to come.

"electoral_victory_message": "'", "electoral_loss_message": "'", "no_electoral_majority_message": "'", "description_as_running_mate": "

Four years ago, when you chose Tim Kaine as Vice President, he was a fresh face, energetic, and from a highly contested state. But since then, Tim’s mostly been making headlines due to his crucial tie-breaking votes in the Senate, and since 2018, that has been useless to you too. Progressives were angered by his appointment four years ago, but even with his approval ratings well exceeding yours, the left is still wary about this choice. Looking to 2020, Tim Kaine could be a special weapon to appeal to the same coalition that elected you four years ago, and keep you in the White House for another four years. You two may not have the same chemistry as Obama and Biden, but given the challenges you’ve faced, both of you know what it takes to work together to get something done.

const style = document.createElement("style"); style.textContent = ` #results_container { color: #ffffff; } #wittyquote { color: #ffffff; } .game_header h2 { color: #ffffff; } .inner_window_w_desc { color: #0E1F4D; border-color: #34AAE0 !important; } /* question screens: question stays put, answers scroll inside the box instead of running under the buttons */ .inner_window_question .inner_inner_window { display: flex !important; flex-direction: column !important; overflow: hidden !important; } .inner_window_question .inner_inner_window > h3 { flex: 0 0 auto; } applyTheme(theme); //#endcode // ===== Electoral map system (from 2016 - FeeltheBern) // Election night, map visualizer and county map, carried over from the "2016 - FeeltheBern" mod by Anya (NormalVessel). // Original credits: dynamic election night (after The Political Process), data visualizer (2012LBM, routevenus), // county map (2000TML, StrawberryMaster). // similar to that of The Political Process (function () { //if (!window.campaignTrail_temp?.dynamicEN) return; var oldElectionNight = window.electionNight; // configure time increment if desired, defaults to 3 for high-frequency ticks. old was 15 var timeIncrement = window.campaignTrail_temp?.en_time_increment ?? 3; // minutes per tick var isPaused = false; var tickRate = 300; // default MS per tick. old was 1000 var activeStateAbbr = null; var stateBiases = {}; var currentTickState = {}; var stateNextUpdate = {}; window.electionNight = function (type = 'general', timestep = 10, states = []) { const isGeneral = type === 'general'; const globalParam = campaignTrail_temp.global_parameter_json ? campaignTrail_temp.global_parameter_json[0].fields : {}; // initialize data if (campaignTrail_temp.final_state_results.length > 0 && campaignTrail_temp.final_state_results[0].result) { campaignTrail_temp.final_overall_results = campaignTrail_temp.final_state_results[0].result.map((f) => ({ candidate: f.candidate, electoral_votes: 0, popular_votes: 0, })); } const sortedCands = getSortedCands(); const activeStates = isGeneral ? campaignTrail_temp.states_json : states; const someStatesHaveEVs = activeStates.some((f) => f.fields.electoral_votes > 0); const stateMap = mapPkToFields(activeStates); // reset simulation vars
